# Temple Scroll Column 57 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 57 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 57:3 — "fear Me" vs. "honor Me"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fear Me" | Literal yir'ah — standard term for reverential fear of God |
| LOGOS | "fear Me" | Same — traditional rendering maintained |
| PNEUMA | "honor Me" | Modern rendering avoiding the connotation of terror |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "fear Me" (EMET/LOGOS). Yir'ah is the standard covenant vocabulary; "honor" dilutes the theological weight. The first-person divine voice makes this especially potent.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 57:6 — "selected-ones" vs. "warriors" vs. "trained soldiers"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "men of war" | Literal 'anshei milchamah |
| LOGOS | "warriors" | Concise English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "trained soldiers" | Modern military terminology |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "warriors" (LOGOS). Concise and accurate; "trained soldiers" (PNEUMA) implies a professional military not necessarily indicated. EMET's "men of war" is acceptable but less natural.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 57:8 — "fearers of God" vs. "God-fearing" vs. "God-fearing"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fearers of God and haters of unjust-gain" | Literal participial forms preserved |
| LOGOS | "God-fearing, who despise dishonest gain" | Standard English adjective/relative clause |
| PNEUMA | "God-fearing, honest, and courageous" | Compressed into simple adjectives |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. Preserves the full Hebrew description while being readable. PNEUMA's compression loses "despise dishonest gain" — an important qualification for the royal guard.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 57:13 — "above them" — scope of royal submission

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his heart shall not be lifted up above them" | Literal — the king must not exalt himself above the council |
| LOGOS | "his heart shall not be exalted above theirs" | Same concept, smoother English |
| PNEUMA | "he must not consider himself above them" | Modern psychological language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The language of the heart being "exalted" preserves the Hebrew idiom (rum lev) while being natural English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 57:15 — monogamy clause phrasing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "she alone shall be with him all the days of her life" | Literal — the wife's lifespan is the duration |
| LOGOS | "she alone shall be with him all the days of her life" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "she alone shall be his companion for life" | Modern phrasing with "companion" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering. "Companion" adds a dimension of mutuality not explicit in the text; the Hebrew simply states she shall be with him for her lifetime. This is a legal restriction on polygamy, not a statement about companionate marriage.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 57:17 — "pervert judgment" vs. "twist justice" vs. scope of prohibitions

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "pervert judgment... a bribe he shall not take" | Literal with inverted Hebrew word order preserved |
| LOGOS | "pervert justice... accept no bribe" | Standard English legal register |
| PNEUMA | "twist justice, accept bribes" | Compressed modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS phrasing. "Pervert justice" is the standard English legal idiom; PNEUMA's "twist" is too informal for legal prohibition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
